migration.lede: Keep your existing OpenAI-shaped calls. Add privacy and routing constraints only when you need them.
migration.agent_prompt:
Migrate this project's LLM calls to TrustedRouter.

1. Read https://trustedrouter.com/llms.txt and
   https://trustedrouter.com/docs/migrate-from-openrouter
2. Point every OpenAI-compatible client at
   https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1 and read the key from
   TRUSTEDROUTER_API_KEY. Keep request and response handling as is.
3. Check every model ID against https://trustedrouter.com/models
   and flag any that are missing.
4. List calls that handle sensitive data and suggest
   provider.min_privacy "zdr" or "confidential" for each.
5. Run the tests, then show me the diff before committing.
migration.agent_hint: Paste into Claude Code, Cursor or Codex.
migration.copy_behavior: Copy on the code panel copies the new version only (removed lines dropped, +/- markers stripped). Agent tab copies the prompt.

verification.headline: Don't trust. Verify.

cards.title: An attested prompt path
cards.body: Prompts travel through a gateway whose build is attested, kept apart from the dashboard and billing systems.
cards.diagram: Your application (OpenAI-compatible request) → encrypted transport → Attested gateway (Prompt path · no content logs) → selected route → Model provider (Provider policy published separately). Below: Dashboard and billing (Control plane): 'Runs separately. Never touches prompt content.'

cards.title: Open source, down to the deploy
cards.body: Gateway, SDKs and deployment configuration are public. Attestation ties that source to the code serving requests.
cards.diagram: Checklist: Read the source / Check the attestation / Match the digest to a commit / Verify it fails closed. Repo chips linked: quill-router, quill-cloud-proxy, quill-cloud-infra, trusted-router-py, trusted-router-js

cards.title: Three clouds, visible fallback
cards.body: Provider and model health are measured continuously, with public latency and availability history.
cards.diagram: GCP · AWS · AZURE, 'fallback stays on the attested path'

cards.title: Fails closed, never quietly downgrades
cards.body: If no route meets your privacy minimum, the request stops before inference instead of falling back to a weaker one.
cards.diagram: deepseek-v4-pro-0813 · min_privacy: "confidential" → only route → Baseten (ZDR · below minimum, struck) → Stopped (Before inference)

faq.headline: What developers ask before routing.
faq.behavior: Accordion; first item open by default; + rotates to ×.
items: A privacy-first AI gateway that routes requests across many providers through one OpenAI-compatible API without logging prompt or output content.
Yes, with an attested prompt path, public source, explicit privacy aliases, and fail-closed behavior as core design constraints.
Do you log prompts or outputs?
No. Prompt and output content are intentionally excluded from the control plane and metadata systems. Optional content export requires explicit destination-level configuration.
The gateway runs in a Trusted Execution Environment and publishes evidence that connects the running image to public source. You can verify that evidence on the trust page.
Can I bring my own provider keys?
Yes. BYOK lets you retain provider commitments or enterprise rate limits while using the TrustedRouter routing and trust boundary.
The gateway fails closed. It does not silently route prompts through an unverified fallback.
Keep the OpenAI SDK, change the base URL, and use the same chat or Responses calls. The migration guide includes tested examples.
